headline: Western Washington stays dry through Wednesday with morning fog and frost; light rain chances return Thursday into late next week.
summary: As of Saturday evening, forecasters expect clouds to clear tonight and winds to ease, so Sunday morning should start with fog, especially in the usual fog-prone spots and river valleys. A weather system approaches the coast late Sunday and Monday, but most of its energy heads south toward California and stays well offshore. Western Washington stays dry, though clouds spread in, and highs Sunday and Monday should be in the mid 50s to low 60s. On Tuesday and Wednesday, high pressure aloft builds over British Columbia while a separate low sits far to the south, off central California. That keeps the region dry, with light winds and clearer skies bringing fog again each morning plus areas of frost, mainly away from the water. A weak trough (a dip in the jet stream) returns Thursday into late next week and brings chances for precipitation. Forecasters say amounts will not be heavy because any front will be weakening as it arrives. Temperatures should stay near normal, with the warmest days around midweek. Confidence is fairly good in the dry stretch through Wednesday and in the pattern change, since computer model ensembles (groups of forecast runs) consistently show the trough returning, but exact timing and amounts were not detailed. No watches, warnings, or advisories were listed.
changes: The forecast was essentially unchanged between the afternoon and evening discussions. The evening update dropped the small Puget Sound convergence zone and the expired marine advisories, and described the Thursday precipitation chance as continuing into late next week rather than only light rain Thursday.

glossary.trough: A dip in the jet stream that often brings cooler, wetter weather.
glossary.convergence zone: An area where air flows together and can form clouds and showers.
glossary.ensembles: Groups of computer forecast runs used to see how much they agree.
glossary.high pressure aloft: A region of sinking air high in the atmosphere that usually brings dry, calm weather.
